Getting Started with CudaMon

Source: vignettes/getting-started.Rmd
getting-started.Rmd

CudaMon monitors NVIDIA GPU activity from R through NVML. A typical session has four steps:

  1. Start the sampler with cm_start().
  2. Run the workload you want to observe.
  3. Add event markers with cm_timestamp() if you want annotated steps.
  4. Stop the sampler, parse the output, and plot the session.

Prerequisites

CudaMon requires:

  • an NVIDIA GPU visible to the current R session
  • a working NVML installation
  • the package installed with its native code compiled successfully

If no GPU is available, the code below is still useful as a reference, but it will not produce samples.

Start a monitoring session

The simplest workflow starts a sampler tied to the current R session. By default, CudaMon samples once per second and includes descendant processes.

library(CudaMon)

sampler <- cm_start()

You can customize the sampling interval or limit collection to a specific device:

sampler <- cm_start(
    period = 0.5,
    device_index = 0
)

Annotate a workload

While the sampler is running, execute the code you want to profile. Use cm_timestamp() to record named events that will later appear as vertical markers in the plot.

cm_timestamp(sampler, "initialization")

Sys.sleep(2)

cm_timestamp(sampler, "training")

Sys.sleep(2)

cm_timestamp(sampler, "evaluation")

Stop and parse the session

When the workload is finished, stop the background sampler and parse the CSV output into a CudaMonSession.

cm_stop(sampler)

session <- cm_parser(sampler)
session
#> CudaMonSession
#>   Device samples: 10
#>   GPU process samples: 0
#>   Event markers: 3
#>   Device metrics path: /tmp/RtmpB0TYTA/cudamon-11983-2ecf59f73d59_device_metrics.csv
#>   Compute processes path: /tmp/RtmpB0TYTA/cudamon-11983-2ecf59f73d59_compute_processes.csv
#>   Events path: /tmp/RtmpB0TYTA/cudamon-11983-2ecf59f73d59_events.csv
#>   Sampler log path: /tmp/RtmpB0TYTA/cudamon-11983-2ecf59f73d59_sampler.log
#>   Root PID: 11983
#>   Include descendants: TRUE

The parsed session contains:

  • device_metrics: device-level GPU samples over time
  • compute_processes: active GPU processes observed during sampling
  • events: event markers recorded with cm_timestamp()
  • paths: the CSV and log files written by the sampler

Visualize GPU activity

Use cm_plot_usage() for the built-in GPU plot.

if (length(session$compute_processes) > 0){
    p <- cm_plot_usage(session, tz = "Europe/Rome")
    p
}

This plot shows device utilization, GPU memory, temperature, and power over time. If you recorded events, they are added as vertical dashed lines.

Complete example 

library(CudaMon)

sampler <- cm_start()

Sys.sleep(2)
cm_timestamp(sampler, "step 1")
Sys.sleep(2)
cm_timestamp(sampler, "step 2")
Sys.sleep(2)
cm_timestamp(sampler, "step 3")
Sys.sleep(2)

cm_stop(sampler)

session <- cm_parser(sampler)
if (length(session$compute_processes) > 0){
    cm_plot_usage(session, tz = "Europe/Rome")
}
